title: Compare integers and absolute value
status: draft: written by Claude, waiting for owner review

hints.int.compare.order: Picture the number line: further right is greater. −3 is to the right of −8, so −3 > −8.
hints.int.compare.abs: Absolute value is the distance from 0, so it's never negative. Work inside the bars first.
hints.int.compare: Further right on the number line is greater. Absolute value is distance from 0.

misconceptionMessages.int.compare-size: With negatives, the bigger the number after the sign, the further left it is, so the smaller it is: −8 < −3.
misconceptionMessages.int.compare-closest-negative: The least is the one furthest left on the number line: the negative furthest from 0.
misconceptionMessages.int.abs-opposite: Absolute value isn't the opposite. It's the distance from 0, so it's never negative: |−7| = 7 and |12| = 12.
misconceptionMessages.int.abs-outside-negative: Only the number inside the bars becomes its distance from 0. A negative sign outside the bars stays: −|−5| = −5.
misconceptionMessages.int.abs-each-first: Work inside the bars first (3 − 8 = −5), then take the absolute value: |−5| = 5.
misconceptionMessages.int.distance-subtracted-sizes: The two numbers are on opposite sides of 0. Add the two distances to 0: from −4 to 6 is 4 + 6 = 10.

sections.title: Compare and order integers
sections.objective: Tell which integer is greater, and order a list.
explain: On a number line, numbers get greater as you go right. Every negative number is less than 0 and less than every positive number.

visual.caption: 3 < 8, but on the other side of 0 the order flips: −3 > −8.

sections.key: Further right is greater. With two negatives, the one closer to 0 is greater: −3 > −8.

worked.note: a negative is less than a positive

sections.title: Absolute value and distance
sections.objective: Find absolute values and the distance between two numbers.
explain: The absolute value of a number is how far it is from 0. Distance is never negative, so |−7| and |7| are both 7.

visual.caption: From −4 to 6 is 10 steps: 4 to get to 0, then 6 more.

sections.key: |n| is the distance from 0. Work inside the bars first. From a negative to a positive, add the two distances to 0.

sections.title: Putting it together
sections.key: Further right is greater. Absolute value is distance from 0, never negative.
